result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.add_duplication_divergence_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Add a graph grown by node duplication with edge loss, a model of protein interaction twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.add_duplication_divergence_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Add a graph grown by node duplication with edge loss, a model of protein interaction title: >- [Graph.add_duplication_divergence_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Add a graph grown by node duplication with edge loss, a model of protein interaction page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add a graph grown by node duplication with edge loss, a model of protein interaction ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L14579-L14678){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.add_duplication_divergence_graph( n, p, seed=None, type=None, label=True, rel=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} networks. ![Duplication-divergence graph](../assets/graphs/add-duplication-divergence-graph.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Three duplication-divergence graphs on a ring of eight nodes, each grown from a single edge by copying a random node and keeping each of the copy's edges with probability p, for p=0.3, 0.6, and 0.9. A copy that keeps no edge is discarded, so the graph stays connected; a higher retention p gives denser graphs with more shared neighbors, 7, 11, and 15 edges here." width="100%"} Starts from two joined nodes and grows to `n`. Each step picks an existing node at random and makes a copy, which keeps each of the original's edges independently with probability `p` and is never joined to the original itself. A copy that keeps no edge is thrown away and the step is retried, so the graph stays connected. Gene duplication followed by divergence works the same way, and the model (Ispolatov, Krapivsky and Yuryev 2005) reproduces the sparse, heavy-tailed, connected networks of protein interactions: small `p` gives sparse, tree-like graphs, and `p` near `1` dense ones. The process is NetworkX's `duplication_divergence_graph()`. In a directed graph every edge points from the earlier-created node to the later one. The graph is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Duplication-divergence graphs are useful for: - modeling protein-protein interaction and gene regulatory networks - growth models where new nodes copy the links of existing ones, as in citation or web link copying - connected, heavy-tailed test graphs ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nodes. Must be at least `2`. [p]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Probability, between `0` and `1`, that a copy keeps each edge of the original. Must be positive when `n > 2`; very small values need many retries. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Integer seed for the random number generator. The same `seed=` with the same other arguments always gives the same graph. If `None` (default), the graph differs on every call. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; a label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `n=` is less than `2`, `p=` is outside `0` to `1`, `p=0` with `n > 2`, or a million copies in a row keep no edge. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} A 200-node graph at `p=0.4` is connected and sparse: ::: {#1e25dbf9 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_duplication_divergence_graph(n=200, p=0.4, seed=1) graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges(), graph.is_connected() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (200, 417, True) ``` ::: ::: Copying makes some nodes hubs while most have one or two neighbors: ::: {#cba14338 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} degrees = graph.get_node_df()["degree"] degrees.median(), degrees.max() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (2.0, 40) ``` ::: :::
